Differences between KJV and other  English versions:												
'======================================												
In the OT, all English versions agree with KJV. In the DC (DeuteroCanon or Apocryphra) there are numerous differences. In the NT, KJV differs from other versions at:												
,												
NA/ SBLG	NET2full/ NRSV	ESV	NIV	KJV	MAPPINGS  * = KJV							
*Act.19:40	Act.19:40-41	Act.19:40-41	Act.19:40-41	Act.19:40-41	Acts.19.40!a=Acts.19.40 & Acts.19.40!b=Acts.19.41							
*2Co.13:12	*2Co.13:12	2Co.13:12-13	2Co.13:12-13	2Co.13:12-13	2Cor.13.12!a=2Cor.13.12 & 2Cor.13.12!b=2Cor.13.13							
*2Co.13:13	*2Co.13:13	2Co.13:14	2Co.13:14	2Co.13:14	2Cor.13.13=2Cor.13.14							
*Php.1:16	*Php.1:16	*Php.1:16	*Php.1:16	Php.1:17	Phil.1.16=Phil.1.17							
*Php.1:17	*Php.1:17	*Php.1:17	*Php.1:17	Php.1:16	Phil.1.17=Phil.1.16							
*3Jn.1:14-15	*3Jn.1:14-15	*3Jn.1:14-15	3Jn.1:14	3Jn.1:14	3John.1.14=3John.1.15!a & 3John.1.15=3John.1.15!b

,												
So, for SBLG  (which has all of these  changes relative to KJV) the mappings are: 												
  "jsword_mappings": [												
    "Acts.19.40!a=Acts.19.40",,												
    "Acts.19.40!b=Acts.19.41",,												
    "2Cor.13.12!a=2Cor.13.12",												
    "2Cor.13.12!b=2Cor.13.13",												
    "2Cor.13.13=2Cor.13.14",												
    "Phil.1.16=Phil.1.17",												
    "Phil.1.17=Phil.1.16",												
    "3John.1.14=3John.1.15!a",												
    "3John.1.15=3John.1.15!b",												
    "Rev.12.18=Rev.13.1!a",												
    "Rev.13.1=Rev.13.1!b"												
    ]												
												
These Mappings correct all the verses marked with  an asterix. 												
NOTES: 												
* The left side is the Source ref and this must be unique, so "!a" etc is added. The right side is the Standard (KJV) ref and does not need to be unique, but "!a" etc is added to help make it humanly readable 												
* These mappings are only added when particular circumstances are true, listed as Tests in the data lines below. 												
* The OT is almost always uniform with KJV versification in the English Bibles, but there is great variety in the OT and NT in Bibles influenced by Hebrew, Greek and Latin traditions. 												
* Occasionally it is better to leave versification uncorrected, as with ESV Rev.12.17. The difference  is equivalent to moving the verse division by a few words, and a correction will merely add confusion.												
* The KJV has other verse divisions which are in a different position in most other Bibles, EG: 												
* The KJV has other verse divisions which are in a different position in most other Bibles, EG: 												
	Mrk.12:15 	NA, ESV	KJV, NRSV, NIV 									
	1Jn.2:14 	NA, NRSV, NIV	KJV, ESV									
KJV starts differently from some Bibles: Mat.15:6; 17.15; 20.5; Mrk.3:20; 12.15; 16.8; Luk.1:74; 6.18; 7.19; Jhn.7:1; Act.2:11; 3.20; 4.6; 5.40; 9.29; 13.39; 24.19; Rom.1:10; 3.26; 7.10; 9.12; 2Co.1:7; 8.14; 10.5; 13.13, 14; Gal.2:20; Eph.1:11; 2.15; 5.14; Php.1:16-17; 2.8; Col.1:22; 1Th.1:3; 2.7, 12; Heb.3:10; 7.21; 12.23; 1Pe.3:16; 1Jn.2:14; Rev.2:28; 12.13; 17.10												
When aligning texts, the following verses are merged becasue they cannot be divided by any rules:  Mat.17:14-15; Mat.20:4-5; Act.4:5-6; Act.24:18-19; Rom.1:9-10; Rom.3:25-26; Rom.7:9-10; 2Co.8:13-14; 2Co.10:4-5; Eph.1:10-11; Eph.2:14-15; Col.1:21-22; 1Th.1:2-3; Heb.3:9-10; Heb.12:22-23; 1Pe.3:15-16; 												
KJV has Colophons without adding verses at: Rom.16:27; 1Co.16:24; 2Co.13:14; Gal.6:18; Eph.6:24; Php.4:23; Col.4:18; 1Th.5:28; 2Th.3:18; 1Ti.6:21; 2Ti.4:22; Tit.3:15; Phm.1:25; Heb.13:25												
												
In the Mappings this is expressed as Source = Standard (ie KJV)												
												
												
												
1) Condensed Version - each section with the Tests to identify the versification being followed, and comparison of numbering in different traditions. This version is easy for humans to understand												
2) Expanded Version - verse-by-verse renumbering to Standard versification with explanatory notes for each verse. This version is easy for use in software to Standardise a Bible or to add notes about Standard versification to a Bible												
     (this version is found below, after the Condensed version and is followed by some more discursive notes)												
												
'=================												
1) CONDENSED VERSION												
'=================												
												
FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:												
'==============												
This datasets has multi-line records divided by "$===========". The first line is a Header with Tests that apply to each subsequent subRecord line. SubRecord lines all start with a tab. 												
												
The columns headed "English", "Hebrew", "Latin", "Greek" and others contain the equivalent versification for Bibles in these traditions. English is determined by NRSV, Hebrew by MT, Latin by Vulgate, Greek by LXX												
Additional columns ("Other") are versions which do not conform to any of these traditions. For example, "Slavonic" follows the Greek tradition except for two passages (Lev.14:55-57; Jos.5:14-6:27). 												
Additional "undivided" columns are supplied for texts where extra text has not been divided into subverses. 												
Some editions of Hebrew, Latin or Greek texts have variations which may conform exactly with another tradition (such as English); if they do not conform with any other tradition their pattern is placed in an additional column. 												
												
References are recorded in the form of Chap:Verse.Subverse, e.g. Gen.6:1.2 is the second subverse of Gen.6:1 which can also be written as Gen.6:1b. In the SourceRef and StandardRef columns it is written Gen.6:1!b because this works with the Mappings for OSIS 												
Subverses can occur when a verse is divided into two or more separate verses in another Bible. EG 2Co.13:12a-b which is 2Co.13:12-13 in some Bibles. The first subverse can also be expresses as 2Co.13:12.1 or 2Co.13:12a or 2Co.13:12!a,												
Subverse also occur, mainly in the LXX, when verses are moved to a different position or even a duplicate position. The moved verses are added as subverses at the end of the previous verse that is numbered in Standard Bibles, so that subsequent verse numbers are not affected.  												
        For example, the moving of 6 verses from Jos.8:30-35 to follow Josh.9:2 in Greek Bibles results in the text of Jos.9:2 gaining 6 subverses. These can be expressed as Jos.9:2*a-b, or Jos.9:2.0-6 or Jos.9:2!0-6. 												
        The original text of Jos.9:2 that occurs before the first additional subverse is referred to as Jos.9:2* or Jos.9:2.0  												
       Such instances occur in LXX at Exo.28:22; Jos.9:2; 1Ki.2:35; 2:46; 5:14; 6:1; 8:53; 9:9; 10:22; 10:26; 12:24; 16:28; Est/Esg.1:1; 3:13; 4:17; 5:1; 8:12; 10:3. ,												
       Duplication of verses occurs in a few places:  1Ki.2:35; 12:24; 16:28. When text is duplicated in this way, some verses may NOT be duplicated, ie: ,												
               1Ki.12:24  has verse that have been duplicated at   1)11:43; 14:22 / 2) 11:26-28 / 3) 11:40 / 4) 11:21-22 / 5) 11:19 / 6) 11:24 / .... / 14) 11:31 / 15) 12:3-5 / 16) 12:6-7 / 17) 12:8-11 / 18) 12:14 / 19) 12:16 / / 21) 12:21 / 22) 12:22-23 / 23) 12:24.0]												
                                 and has verses that have been move at  7) 14:1-2 / 8) 14:3 / 9) 14:4 / 10) 14:6 / 11) 14:12 / 12) 14:11 / 13) 14:17-18 / / 20) 12:17; 												
               1Ki.2:35  has verse that have been duplicated at   1) 4:29 .2=4:30 / / 4) 5:15 / 5) 7:23 / / 11) 2:8.1 / 12) 2:8.2 / 13) 2:8.3 / 14) 2:9,												
                                 and has verses that have been move at   3) 3:1 / / 6) 9:24 / 7) 9:25 / 8) 9:23.1 / 9) 9:23.2 / 10) 9:23.3,												
,												
"Absent" means that there is a verse in Standard versification that has no text, so when creating a Standard Bible, this verse number has to be created, with a footnote saying that some Bibles have no text here. 												
 - It is marked as "Absent [=Ref.n:n] if  the text of this verse exists elsewhere in the Source. If it is merged with that verse, it is actioned with Merge Verse. If it exists on its own with a different verse number, it is actioned with Renumber Verse & IfEmpty verse. ,												
 - It is marked as "Absent [Ref.n:n] if the Source has an empty verse at this point. The reference indicates this empty verse is numbered in the Source. This is actioned with Renumber Verse ,												
 - It is marked as "Absent" without any ref if the source simply lacks this verse. This is actioned with Empty Verse. ,												
												
												
 TEST: 												
These examine the points at which the traditions are different. They can be used to determine which tradition is being followed in a specific Bible. 												
English Bibles follow mostly the Hebrew tradition, with some differences. Because so many Bibles and most commentaries follow this same set of differences, 												
English standard is defined by the NRSV which is virtually the same as KJV with one added verse break and two removed.												
       Comparing NRSV=KJV: 2Cor.13:12=13:12-13 so 2Cor.13:13=13:14; 3Jn.1:15=3Jn.1:14b; Rev.12:18=13:1a												
       (v.18 contains the phrase "And he stood on thje sand by the sea".  Some Bibles eg ESV have this phrase at the end of v.17; most Bibles eg KJV, NIV have it at the start of 13:1; a few Bibles eg HCSB, NLT, follow NRSV and put it in a new v.18)												
East-European or Orthodox Bibles tend to follow the Greek traditions, and West-European or Catholic Bibles tend to follow the Latin tradition. Jewish translations tend to follow the Hebrew tradition. 												
However, many Bibles employ a mixture of traditions by following English, Hebrew, Latin or Greek traditional versification for different sections of the Bible. 												
												
Each section has at least 4 columns:  versification numbers in the Standard English, traditional Hebrew, traditional Latin and traditional Greek (and occasionally others)												
A Bible is following the numbering in a specific column if the tests above that column are TRUE for that Bible. They may be true for more than one column if these have identical versification. 												
* Ref.1:30=Last	is TRUE if the Bible has exactly 30 verses in chapter "REF.1"											
* Ref.1:30=Exist	is TRUE if the Bible has a verse numbered 30 with text in it											
* Ref.1:30.2=Exist	is TRUE if the Bible has at least 3 subverses in Ref.1:30 (the verse that appears in all Bibles is subverse 0)											
* Ref.1:30=NotExist	is TRUE if the Bible does not have a verse numbered 30 with text in it (and there IS text in the previous verse, if this isn't v.1 - i.e. this chapter didn't end earlier)											
* Ref.1:30.2=NotExist	is TRUE if the Bible has fewer than 2 subverses in Ref.1:30											
* Ref.1:30>Ref.1:29	is TRUE if the Bible has more words in Ref.1:30 than in Ref.1:29 (this test is designed with enough leeway to work for whatever language the Bible is written in)											
* Ref.1:30<Ref.1:29	is TRUE if the Bible has fewer words in Ref.1:30 than in Ref.1:29 											
* Ref.1:30<Ref.1:29*2	is TRUE if the Bible has fewer words in Ref.1:30 than twice the number of words in Ref.1:29											
* Ref.1:30<Ref.1:29.0	is TRUE if the Bible has fewer words in Ref.1:30 than in the subverse '0' (i.e. the text which is found in all Bibles, whether or not subverses are added) 											
	(subverse 0 is identical to the text found in all Bibles. Additional text that occurs in some Bibles is put into subverse 1 onwards. There are no tests for the length of those subverses because the text may not be divided into subverses)											
TextBeforeV1	is TRUE if there is canonical text (ie a Psalm Title) before the verse code of v.1												
												
ALIGNMENTS:												
Different types of alignment are created by various situations: 												
												
OT: 												
SubdividedVerse	occurs when an English verse contains the text of more than one verse in another Bible, e.g. Exo.28:29  (formerly called 'Concatenation')											
MergedVerse	occurs when an English is empty because it is merged with another verse in another Bible e.g. Gen.50:22-23. The Ref in square brackets is where the merged text is found.   (formerly called 'DuplicateTarget')											
OneToOne	occurs when a difference causes this and often subsequent verses to be displaced , e.g. Num.12:16--13:33											
LongVerse	refers to a section of LXX or Vulgate which is inserted into Standard versification as a series of subverses, e.g. 1Ki.6:1.0-4 (subverse "0" is the normal text of the verse, and 1-4 are additional subverses) 											
LongVerseElsewhere	occurs where text has been moved into a LongVerse elsewhere, e.g. Jos.8:30-35											
LongVerseElsewhereJoin	occurs where text from PART of a verse has been moved into a LongVerse elsewhere, e.g. Exo.37:1, 2.1											
LongVerse/LVElsewhere	occurs where a LongVerse has been created by moving text from elsewhere, e.g. Jos.9:2 											
LongVerseDuplicated	occurs where text has been duplicated in a LongVerse elsewhere, i.e. duplicated from LXX 1Ki.2:35; 12:24; 16:28											
LongVerse/LVDuplicated	occurs where a LongVerse contains text that also occurs elsewhere, e.g. i.e. LXX 1Ki.2:35, 46; 12:24; 16:28											
LongVerse/LVExtra	occurs where a LongVerse has been created by adding text to the text, e.g. Est/Esg.1:1. These may alternatively occur as extra chapters. 											
TextMayBeMissing	occurs where some ancient versions do not include any words, e.g. Neh.7:68											
StartDifferent	occurs where verse divisions can occur in slightly different positions, e.g. Num.26:1											
[= REF]	indicates an alternate way to refer to the same verse in the same Bible											
												
												
NT: 												
TextMayBeMissing	occurs where some ancient manuscripts do not include any words in a verse, e.g. Mat.12:47											
PassageMoved	occurs only at Rom.16:25-27 which is found at Rom.14:24-26 in some manuscripts 											
Colophon	occurs at the end of epistles, which have a verse about provenance in some manuscripts, e.g. 1Co.16:24											
PassageMissing	occurs at the start of passages that are missing in some manuscripts, i.e. Mrk.9:20 & Jhn.7:53--8:11 (& 1Jn.5:7b-8a which does not alter any versification)											
StartDifferent	occurs where verse divisions can occur in slightly different positions, e.g. Rev.13:1 											
SubdividedVerse	occurs when one verse merges more than one verse in another Bible, e.g. 3Jn.1:14-15]											
MergedVerse												
Occasionally the differences result in a change to verse order. This is marked by an asterix in the top row, e.g."Greek*". This occurs only in Latin "Sir" and in Greek at  Exo.20:13-15; 21.16-17; 35:8-27; 37:1--38:31; 39:32-42; 40:30-31; Num.1:24-25; 10:34; 26:15-47; Jos.24:31; 1Ki.3:1; 4:20-21, 25-28; 6:1; 7:1-12, 21, 25; 9:16, 23-25; 11:5-8; 22:46-49; Jer.31:37; 49:7-39; Ezk.7:3-5; Mal.4:6; (using English verse numbers)												
,												
REFs 	THese are based on SIL/UBS as in Paratext and USX, with the addition of Ade for AddEsth. They are the first 3 characters of the book name except for: Jdg, Sng, Ezk, Jol, Nam, Mrk, Jhn, Php, Phm, Jas, 1Jn, 2Jn, 3Jn,											
	ESTHER can be tagged as Est.1-10a OR Est.1-16 OR  Ade.10b-16 OR possibly as Esg.1-16 (which should only be used if the Bible has both Hebrew and Greek Esther). The following assumes that Ade has only 10b-16, and it maps Esg to Est unless Est also exists. ,

'=========================================================================================================================================												
												
'=================												
2) EXPANDED VERSION 												
'=================												
												
												
FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:												
'==============												
SourceType	This isn't used in programming but is useful for checking. It is the type of Bible versification being followed on this line, and selected by the Tests at the end.											
SourceRef	This is a verse number in a Bible being tested and/or converted. 											
StandardRef	This is the equivalent verse number in a Standard Bible IF the tests at the end are TRUE											
Action	This is what you do with the text in the verse found in the Source (See "How to use this" at Tinyurl.com/VersificationHowTo)											
Importance & NoteMarker	"Nec." = Necessary - ie a note which is always needed because the verse number has changed. 											
	"Opt." = Optional - ie a note which is not needed if Versification is used because each verse retains its own number code and aligns using Mappings (only available in STEPBible)											
	"Acd." = useful in Bibles used by academics who want to know all differences in ancient Bibles. 											
	"Inf." = useful in any Bible, to explain why verses are empty, but shouldn't be added to Bibles that already have notes about this (CHECK for a note at Act.15:34 which is the verse most likely to be absent.)											
	(n) = the StandardRef which may be the same as the SourceRef 											
	^n = the SourceRef if this is different to the StandardRef 											
	^[n] = an alternate ref when the SourceRef and StandardRef are identical											
	"[1]" etc are suggested markers for the note. It is normally the verse number of the most important alternate version. The chapter number is included if it is different to the chapter in the StandardRef											
Notes	Standard phrases are used (listed at the end) bounded by "%" to aid replacement by translated phrases.											
Reversification Note 	This is the text of a note that is suited to a Bible that has been reversified with codes for StandardRef. followed by its own ref in bold when different. 											
Versification Note 	This is the text of a note that is suited to a Bible that keeps its own verse numbers  followed by StandardRef in brackets when different. 											
Ancient Versions 	This is a list of the refs as occurring in traditional Hebrew, Latin & Septuagint editions.  It is only useful in Bibles used by academics. 											
Tests	These tests have to be TRUE. If they aren't, move on to the next line. There's a section at the end doesn't have any tests, so it applies to that verse in every Bible version. 											
												
See notes at the end on how it works, but briefly, for the line: 												
	Gen.32:1	Gen.31:55	Renumber verse	Nec. (55)^32:1	%Normally in this Bible the verse numbering here is% 32:1.		(Hebrew=32:1 • Latin=31:55 • Greek=31:55)	Gen.32:33=Last				
This means: 												
at Gen.32:1: if Gen.32:33=Last (ie if v.33 is the last verse in Gen.32) then:												
* renumber the verse as Gen.31:55												
* optionally add a note: [1] "Normally in this Bible the verse numbering here is 32:1 (Hebrew=32:1 • Latin=31:55 • Greek=31:55)"												
(This note is optionally added to Bibles likely to be used with English commentaries. The bracketted  'Hebrew/Latin/Greek'  is only included in Bibles likely to be used by academics.)

Phrases and Abbreviations to translate to different languages: 												
'=====================================================================================================================												
VERSIFICATION												
This adds the Versification note (if there is one) without changing any verse numbers, and relies on code in STEPBible Mappings to align them with Standard Bibles. 												
For most Bibles, process only "Nec." lines.  Wording in the notes include: 												
REF %in most Bibles%	[when SourceRef differs from StandardRef]											
REF %in some Bibles%	[when SourceRef differs from StandardRef in Apoc. books because Bibles vary]											
After versification, look for any Empty verses and add a note: %This verse is empty in this translation%												
												
For Academic Bibles, process also the "Opt." and "Acd." lines. This includes additional notes												
Also at REF in some Bibles	[for duplications in LXX]											
REF %in some Bibles%	[giving AltRef when SourceRef is same as StandardRef]											
BK.REF %in some Bibles%	[giving AltRef when SourceRef is same as StandardRef]											
BK names abbreviations used:  	2Ch. Man. Dan. Sus. Bel. Bar. LJe.											
Some of the following notes may be used in Acd. texts												
												
REVERSIFICATION												
This adds the Reversification note and adds Standard verse numbers before the Source verse number so that it aligns with Standard Bibles												
For most Bibles, process the "Nec." and "Opt." notes. For Academic Bibles process also the "Acd." notes.  Wording in the notes include: 												
%Normally in this Bible this verse and the next occur as one verse that is numbered% REF.

%As normal in this Bible the text for this verse is included at% REF.

%Normally in this Bible similar text is also found at% REF.

%In some Bibles this verse may contain text similar to% REF.
